findings.title: Gathering With Closed Reception
findings.claim: The face-first gathering becomes a counter-scene to the pericope's responsive lowering: the knowledgeable receive recitation, fall, speak, weep, and grow in humility, while the focus group is gathered unable to see, speak, or hear. The closing denial of a protective wali leaves their abode without a rival guardian.
findings.mechanism: Focus guidance, misguidance, gathering, face, impaired faculties, and abode meet the responses in 17:107-109 and the denied wali in 17:111. Voluntary, voiced lowering changes the focus into a coerced closed-reception scene.
findings.reader_payoff: The same lowered posture can mark chosen response or imposed humiliation; capacities and destination distinguish them.
findings.containment: The groups are not identified as the same people, impairments remain bodily, and the comparison does not prove deliberate one-to-one antithesis. The refuge/wali echo is bounded.

epistemic.reason: Trusted channel evidence names the focus branches; exact pericope occurrences ground the contacts, while their synthesis remains interpretive.

findings.title: A Lull That Renews the Blaze
findings.claim: Every lull in the focus fire is answered by added blaze; 17:109 applies the same increase operation to humility. In this pericope increase has different objects: inward humility deepens, while each focus abatement is met by renewed fire.
findings.mechanism: The every-time construction links خَبَتْ to زِدْنَٰهُمْ and سَعِيرًا. 17:109's increase of خُشُوعًا makes that operation meet another result, distinguishing the punitive cycle from increase as such.
findings.reader_payoff: A momentary decrease is not release, and increase itself has no single moral direction.
findings.containment: The comparison does not transfer humility to the fire or turn the fire into a metaphor. The passages may be parallel rather than deliberate antithesis.

epistemic.reason: Trusted branch and channel evidence supports abatement and renewed burning; the 17:109 contrast is a contextual inference.

findings.mechanism: The focus gathering meets 17:103-104's expulsion, drowning, restored dwelling, arrival, and collective joining. These movements change a generic forced procession into the end of a local contest over who can displace, settle, and gather a people.
findings.reader_payoff: The resurrection gathering becomes one end of a sequence about who determines where a people stand and where they are brought.
findings.containment: This is a spatial parallel, not an identity between the groups or a literal forecast. The historical reversal and final gathering may remain parallel.

epistemic.reason: The legacy_unbound trace's focus and context coordinates match supplied occurrences; the spatial synthesis remains attributed.

findings.title: Two Descents, Two Increases
findings.claim: The pericope places two downward postures side by side: the knowledgeable fall on their chins, speak, weep, and grow in humility; the focus group is gathered on its faces without sight, speech, or hearing, and its increase is blaze. The shared descent and increase operations have different objects and responses.
findings.mechanism: Focus face, muteness, deafness, and increase meet contextual chin, prostration, speech, tears, humility, and increase. The contact distinguishes chosen receptive lowering from coerced descent and makes the object of increase part of the contrast.
findings.reader_payoff: Posture alone does not determine what a downward movement means; ability to receive and respond changes the scene.
findings.containment: This attributed structure is not proof of a deliberate one-to-one antithesis. The focus remains bodily punishment; the prostration passage may be a neighboring image.

epistemic.reason: The HFT word coordinates and roots match the focus and 17:107-109 occurrences; its contrast and alternative remain attributed.

findings.title: A Path Between Voice and Silence
findings.claim: The focus's guidance, blocked speech, and blocked hearing meet 17:110's prayer instruction: invocation is bounded by raised voice and vanishing speech, and a way between them is sought. Guidance can be heard as a communicative course, while the focus group can neither send nor receive.
findings.mechanism: Focus direction and sensory losses meet invocation, vocal endpoints, seeking, a middle, and path. Their contact makes the focus's impairment the collapse of a channel that the neighboring verse calibrates.
findings.reader_payoff: The path can be the route by which address remains audible and receivable.
findings.containment: 17:110 may regulate prayer etiquette without describing the eschatological group or addressing those made astray.

epistemic.reason: All HFT context coordinates and roots match; the communication reading remains attributed with its etiquette-only alternative.

findings.title: Creaturely Need and Divine Sovereignty
findings.claim: The focus's astray seek plural protectors; the closing ayah denies God a partner in sovereignty and a wali arising from abasement. Their shared wali relation makes creaturely protection a need that does not reverse onto the sovereign who guides and gathers.
findings.mechanism: The focus support-seeking wali branch meets 17:111's co-sharer in dominion, wali from abasement, and command to magnify. The relation changes missing protectors into a contrast between vulnerable creatures and a sovereign who needs none.
findings.reader_payoff: The plural search for help and the closing denial of divine need become sides of an asymmetrical relation.
findings.containment: Shared wali vocabulary may connect adjacent claims without defining one theory of guardianship. The focus can simply state that the astray find no protectors besides God.

epistemic.reason: Exact focus and 17:111 coordinates match; the legacy_unbound relation and its alternative remain attributed.

findings.title: A Fire Cycle Without the Middle
findings.claim: As an exploratory structural echo, every focus fire lull is answered by added blaze. In 17:110 prayer is kept between raised voice and near-extinction; the contrast makes the focus's renewal perceptible as a cycle that refuses the communicative middle.
findings.mechanism: Focus abatement, increase, and blaze meet the attributed fire branch in the prayer term, vocal endpoints, and a sought middle. Their contact suggests an anti-median regulator: every approach to low intensity is sent upward again.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus increase becomes a rule about what the fire cycle does whenever it nears quiet.
findings.containment: This is a speculative cross-domain analogy, not a claim that prayer means fire. The prayer verse may regulate etiquette without commenting on punishment.

epistemic.reason: Coordinates match the supplied surfaces, but the prayer/fire branch is unresolved and the structural analogy is explicitly exploratory.

findings.title: Guidance Asked and Guidance Named
findings.claim: Under the supplied Fātiḥa lens, the request to be guided to the straight path meets 17:97's statement that the one Allah guides is guided; the path prayer's boundary against straying meets the focus's misguidance clause and its stated consequence. The focus reads as conditional outcome beside petition.
findings.mechanism: Focus guidance and misguidance carry the relation. 1:6 supplies a first-person request and named straight path; 1:7 distinguishes that path from the lost. This act of asking changes the focus's paired clauses from abstract classification into petition and outcome.
findings.reader_payoff: The prayer and the focus statement about guided and misled people remain connected without erasing the judgment scene.
findings.containment: This overlay does not claim 17:97 quotes or formally answers the Fātiḥa. It uses only supplied 1:6-7 occurrences; 1:2-5 adds no part of this finding.

epistemic.reason: The Arabic and root occurrences support the contacts; petition-to-outcome is an inference, and the packet gives no trust label for these context projections.
